name: Tree Queries
description: Those who don't work don't eat. Get the things you want with your own power. But believe, the earnest and serious people are the ones who have the last laugh... But even then, I won't give you a present. —Santa, Hayate no Gotoku! Since Hayate didn't get any Christmas presents from Santa, he is instead left solving a tree query problem. Hayate has a tree with $$$n$$$ nodes. Hayate now wants you to answer $$$q$$$ queries. Each query consists of a node $$$x$$$ and $$$k$$$ other additional nodes $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$. These $$$k+1$$$ nodes are guaranteed to be all distinct. For each query, you must find the length of the longest simple path starting at node $$$x^\dagger$$$ after removing nodes $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$ along with all edges connected to at least one of nodes $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$. $$$^\dagger$$$ A simple path of length $$$k$$$ starting at node $$$x$$$ is a sequence of distinct nodes $$$x=u_0,u_1,\ldots,u_k$$$ such that there exists a edge between nodes $$$u_{i-1}$$$ and $$$u_i$$$ for all $$$1 \leq i \leq k$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of nodes of the tree and the number of queries. The following $$$n - 1$$$ lines contain two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$, $$$u \ne v$$$) — denoting an edge between nodes $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. The following $$$q$$$ lines describe the queries. Each line contains the integers $$$x$$$, $$$k$$$ and $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$ ($$$1 \leq x \leq n$$$, $$$0 \leq k \lt n$$$, $$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) — the starting node, the number of removed nodes and the removed nodes. It is guaranteed that for each query, $$$x,a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$$$ are all distinct. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$k$$$ over all queries will not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each query, output a single integer denoting the answer for that query.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1904E — Tree Queries [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
